newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic wins go-ahead on ISDN pricing.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic wins go-ahead on ISDN pricing.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said a Delaware county court judge had temporarily approved the firm's rate plan for Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) telephone service in the state.

The company said Monday that Kent County Superior Court Judge N. Maxson Terry granted permission for it to proceed with its new pricing plan while he reviews the company's appeal of a July 2 rate order by the Delaware regulators.
Bell Atlantic had asked the judge to allow the company to charge the rates it proposed April 17 to the Delaware Public Service Commssion (PUC).

The company's proposal would reduce current rates by 15 to 86 percent for residential ISDN, a service that provides high-speed access to the Internet, on-line services and corporate computer networks.
On August 9, the court stayed a Delaware state regulatory order that had set a $28.02 flat rate for residential ISDN service, the company said.
In his ruling, Judge Terry said Bell Atlantic-Delaware may bill customers at lower rates as of August 1, 1996.
The schedule calls for charges of $31 for 20 hours of ISDN service per month, $60 for 140 hours and ranges up to $248 per month for unlimted ISDN access.
Customers would receive credits for the lower rates back to Aug. 1 at a future date, the company said.
As a result of the court-ordered stay, introductory rates that were implemented in November 1995 had remained in effect while the court considered the company's appeal of the PSC decision.
